children: Indonesian state-owned plantation firm Agrinas Palma Nusantara currently has 3 million hectares (11,583 square miles) of land under its control after handing over 1 million hectares to fellow state enterprise Perhutani, the company's chief executive said on Monday.

By May, a government task force had transferred 4.12 million hectares of land to Agrinas, a company established in 2025, after seizing the areas from firms accused of violating forest-use regulations.
On Monday, Agrinas' chief executive Mohammad Abdul Ghani told an industry discussion panel that they had handed over 1 million hectares of industrial forest concessions to Perhutani.
"Agrinas only has 3 million. Of those 3 million, the oil palm plantations are currently undergoing verification. At most, there are 800,000 hectares of oil palm," Ghani said.
He said Agrinas has also been instructed to expand the area of its palm oil plantations by 400,000 hectares in Indonesia's easternmost region of Papua.
"I have proposed to the President that the 'plasma scheme' to be funded by the BPDP should be developed there. The land is already available," Ghani said.

He was referring to a partnership scheme between a plantation company and surrounding smallholder farmers, where the company typically provides planting materials and technical assistance and buys the farmers' harvest. BPDP is Indonesia's plantation fund agency, responsible for collecting and distributing levies from palm oil and cocoa bean exports.
Ghani did not give any estimate on the amount of investment needed for the expansion.
The plantation fund was set up to finance the replanting of smallholdings, and is aimed at improving yields while maintaining plantation sizes, according to a related regulation.
